targetAudience.primary: Agent-runtime, digital-employee and AI governance engineers designing delegated worker roles
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands agent roles, configuration inheritance and capability permissions.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A role intended for specialization can accidentally become a second authority plane, especially when a worker is resumed or reconstructed.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change projects role files through a typed override set, preserves parent-owned authority-bearing configuration, permits bounded capability reduction and applies the same constrained path on cold resume.

externalHook.description: Behavioral specialization is useful only when the child cannot turn its role file into a new permission, routing or infrastructure authority.

coreProposition: Delegated agent roles should be monotonic authority deltas under an inherited maximum authority envelope: they may specialize declared behavior and reduce bounded capabilities, but authority-bearing configuration must remain inherited across spawn, resume and reconstruction.

originalValue.description: Frames role configuration as an ordered authority transformation, separating behavioral delta, capability reduction and explicit capability expansion rather than treating every role setting as equivalent configuration.

readerTakeaway: Define a typed, allowlisted role delta; prove child authority never exceeds the inherited envelope; and require a separate approved event for any capability expansion.

supported: The merged Codex implementation projects role files into typed AgentRoleOverrides.
Regression tests preserve parent permissions, provider configuration, approval reviewer, MCP servers, base URL and notifications against hostile role settings.
Selected role-controlled capabilities are reduction-oriented; managed requirements remain effective.
Symlinked user role files are rejected and cold resume uses the bounded role path.
unsupported: Runtime containment of every tool call or external effect
uncertain: How schema evolution automatically identifies new authority-bearing fields
How explicit child capability expansion should be represented and approved

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article concerns a general delegation invariant and does not require a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged implementation gives concrete mechanism-level evidence, while the Research Object contributes a reusable and bounded authority model for delegated agents.
